intro: Italian and Brazilian, living in Copenhagen. I like things that touch the physical world, whether that is a wind turbine, a guitar string, or a mountain pass at five thousand metres.

entries: Building fast data acquisition and edge controls for wind and solar plants.
Learning John Mayer songs on the acoustic, slowly and badly.
Reading my way through the books my dad left behind.
Rebuilding this site, one argument with myself at a time.

sections.title: Where I come from
sections.body: Two passports, three countries. Born and raised in Brazil, Italian by descent, Danish by postcode. Most of what I find interesting sits somewhere in the overlap, in the gap between how things are supposed to work and how they actually behave once they are outdoors and it is raining.

sections.title: Guitar
sections.body: Acoustic, mostly. I am working through John Mayer, which is a humbling way to spend an evening. Progress is measured in how few times I have to stop.

sections.title: Mountains
sections.body: The hardest thing I have done is the Ausangate circuit in Peru, five days around a mountain with two Italians who somehow spoke Portuguese. There is a post about it on the blog. I would do it again tomorrow.

sections.title: Keeping score
sections.body: Creatine every morning, an X on the calendar hanging off a single screw on the electrical panel in my kitchen. The Sports page counts the rest, in pizzas.

sections.title: Ragnarok
sections.body: The game of my childhood, and now a server I run for friends split between Denmark and Brazil. It is in the portfolio, because the game was never the hard part.
